title: Advancement of Nanoengineered Flavonoids for Chronic Metabolic Diseases
abstract: The increasing occurrence of chronic metabolic diseases (CMDs) presents a substantial public health challenge worldwide, necessitating the development of pioneering therapeutic approaches. Flavonoids, which are naturally occurring compounds, exert a broad spectrum of biological activities, encompassing their anti-inflammatory, anti-diabetic, and antioxidant properties, among others. Though they have a potential role in treating CMDs, they face challenges in their extraction and purification, poor gastrointestinal absorption, low solubility, and rapid metabolism, which impede their clinical applicability. Nanotherapeutics has been receiving significant attention as it aids in resolving these issues. Hence, the purpose of this chapter is to shed light on the advances in different nanoengineered formulations of flavonoids. The chapter commences with an outline of chronic metabolic diseases, emphasizing their prevalence and the pressing need for innovative therapeutics strategies to address this burden. Following this, the role of flavonoids in chronic metabolic conditions is discussed. Moreover, the chapter also elucidates on nanoengineering strategies for accomplishing efficient flavonoid delivery, with a particular emphasis on versatile nanoformulations, such as liposomes, solid lipid nanoparticles, and phytosomes. Next, we discuss optimization techniques, encompassing surface modification strategies to enhance targeting and stability, controlled release approaches for sustained therapeutic effects, and the potential synergistic outcomes. The enhancement of the bioavailability and stability of flavonoids is addressed, encompassing strategies to overcome gastrointestinal barriers, targeted delivery approaches for site-specific action, and methods to prevent flavonoid degradation. Subsequent sections elucidate the potential of nanoengineered flavonoids in managing chronic metabolic diseases, focusing on obesity, diabetes, and cardiovascular disorders. The mechanisms of action and the impact of nanoengineered delivery systems on efficacy are highlighted, providing valuable insights. It highlights the challenges involved in their clinical applicability and discusses innovative strategies to overcome these issues.”
